Each phase ends in an all-reduce over all 72 GPUs, so every phase waits for the slowest GEMM. The step therefore pays σ·E[max over 72 of |Z|] on each of the 16 GEMMs.

- The jitter-free compute time is 16 × T_gemm. The overhead per phase is T_gemm × 0.05 × E[max₇₂ |Z|].
- The 16 phases cancel in the ratio, so overhead % = 5 × E[max₇₂ |Z|].
- To estimate E[max₇₂ |Z|], take the median of the maximum. It solves 2(1−Φ(x)) = 1 − 0.5^(1/72) ≈ 0.0096, which gives x ≈ 2.59.
- The mean of the maximum sits about 0.08 above the median (Gumbel correction), so E[max₇₂ |Z|] ≈ 2.67.
- Overhead ≈ 5 × 2.67 ≈ 13.4%.

I did not run the simulator or the `tail_latency` tool for this. The figure comes from the closed form above and a hand estimate of the extreme-value statistics. The all-reduce time is not in the denominator, since the question asks for a percentage of the compute time only.
